newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Two more S.Korean bankers probed over Hanbo loans.
newsitem.headline: Two more S.Korean bankers probed over Hanbo loans.

text.p: South Korea's state prosecutors on Thursday summoned two more leading bankers over massive loans to insolvent Hanbo Steel Co, a prosecution official said.
He said Chang Myung-son, president of the Korea Exchange Bank, and Kim Shi-hyung, head of the state-run Korea Development Bank, were being questioned on whether they were involved in irregularities.
"The two bankers were summoned to the prosecution office this morning," the official told reporters.
On Wednesday, the prosecutors arrested the heads of two other leading banks -- Sheen Kwang-shik of Korea First Bank and Woo Chan-mok of Cho Hung Bank -- on charges of bribery.

The four banks are the main creditors of Hanbo Steel, South Korea's second largest steelmaker, which was declared insolvent on January 23 after accumulating about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans.
Lee Chong-yeon, a former Cho Hung Bank president, was also being questioned by the prosecutors, the official said.

Prosecution investigators have probed over a lobbying fund kept by Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo, who was arrested last Friday on charges of fraud and violating laws on cheques and trust and savings companies.

Chung, famous for extravagant spending habits and lobbying skills, built up South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate by rapidly expanding the steelmaking flagship and acquiring or setting up 18 companies during the past three years.
Prosecutors said they had also examined 175 bank accounts belonging to Chung, his relatives and the conglomerate to check for irregularities.
Prosecutors have accused Sheen and Woo of taking 400 million won ($460,000) each from Chung in return for huge loans from their banks.
Senior prosecutor Choi Byung-koog said Chung was still being grilled on whether he provided kickbacks to others, including politicians.

On Wednesday, a prominent opposition member of parliament, Kwon Roh-kap, said he had accepted between 150 million and 160 million won ($173,000 and $184,000) from Chung, partly to fund an election campaign.
Kwon, the first politician to admit taking money from Chung, is a close associate of Kim Dae-jung, leader of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics.
The opposition has alleged that top aides to President Kim Young-sam peddled influence for the massive loans to Hanbo Steel. Kwon said he had nothing to do with the loans.
Political analysts said the Hanbo scandal could have a serious impact on presidential elections in December.
President Kim, who ordered a probe into the loans last week, has called the scandal a typical example of corruption.
Kim is barred from running for a second term but he is believed to be trying to extend his influence by installing a protege in office.
